messages.subject: Issue related to define.sliders
parts:
As a new user of the geomorph package, I'm struggling with the define.sliders function. 

dt <- readland.tps("AppendFilesCurves.tps", specID="imageID", readcurves=TRUE) #Importing dataset 

#Defining sliders as follows using the auto-mode : a vector of 50 landmarks with 48 landmarks identified as semi-landmarks, thus landmarks 1 and 50 identified as fixed landmarks. 
slide <- define.sliders(c(1:50), 48)#defining sliders 

#Message error when trying to perform a GPA
gpa <- gpagen(dt, curves=slide, ProcD=F)#Using bending energy
Error in La.svd(MY, k, k) : infinite or missing values in 'x'

Am I getting something wrong in my definition of the sliders file ? 
Thanks in advance, 


         Laurent Pallas.
           PhD. Student

messages.author: 511e44c7d1e1bab0
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Issue related to define.sliders
parts:
Laurent,

this is not an issue of define.sliders, but rather a formatting problem in your original tps file, and specifically in the scale arguments of some specimens. For individuals 11 and 23 (codes Pygathrix_119648 Rhinopithecus_19502) the scale value in the tps file uses comma instead of point for the decimal mark. Because of that, geomorph does not read it in correctly, the coordinates cannot be scaled, and they are transformed to NAs, which is then causing the rest of your issues.

Your slider definition is OK, so the only thing you need to do is review your original file. I changed the commas to points manually and was able to run the rest of your script without problems, but probably you should review that file more generally, as the magnitude of those two scaling factors also looks off.

Hope this helps!

Antigoni
